title: The Threefold Authority Order: Tier-1, Tier-0, and Tier-2 in Canon, Protocol, and Translation

tier_1: Meaning of Tier-1: reserved kernel symbols, exact identities, and the immutable namespace; Tier-1 authority is positive as well as prohibitive and does not by itself execute a run, audit a ledger, validate a closure, or repair a translation.
tier_0: Meaning of Tier-0: protocol, contracts, validators, closures, ledgers, seam accounting, and stance derivation; Tier-0 does not authorize by itself.
Promotion limits: usefulness, fluency, or public explanation does not become canon, protocol, proof, or final stance by itself; Tier-2 does not authorize by itself.

source_role: Official authority-axis reference; defines Tier-1/Tier-0/Tier-2 roles and promotion limits (handoff manifest; source front matter).
scope: The threefold authority order governing what may define, execute, validate, translate, extend, adopt, or preserve within the corpus. Functional systems govern the kind of work; authority tiers govern the kind of authority.
non_goal: Does not specify the operating grammar of UMCP, RCFT, or ULRC (cite the Operating System papers for those); authority placement does not itself perform evaluation, discovery, or translation.
notes: Shared packet DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21212668 (coordinated four-paper release); the DOI identifies the archive, the record identifies the member work.
